import json, os, tempfile
with open('/spec/formal-context.json') as f:
    data=json.load(f)
p='Research.BinaryTreeReduction.'
obj={
 'schema_version':1,
 'candidate_hash':data['candidate_hash'],
 'status':'complete',
 'statement':'For every floating-point model M consisting of a real u >= 0 and a function r: R -> R such that for every real z there exists a real delta with |delta| <= u and r(z) = z(1 + delta), the construction takes a finite binary tree with real pairs at its leaves, replaces each pair (x,y) by r(xy), and recursively combines child results by r(a+b). If d is the tree depth (a leaf has depth 0, and a node has depth 1 + max of its child depths) and (d+1)u < 1, its result is the exact sum of the leaves of some tree with the same shape as the input, whose corresponding leaf values differ from the exact products xy by at most gamma(d+1,u)|xy|, where gamma(k,u) = (ku)/(1-ku) for natural k, interpreted in the reals. Another target states that the actual tree of rounded products itself has corresponding leaf errors at most u|xy|. The remaining targets identify the defining equations for the rounded product term, rounded product tree, and model multiplication. The existential perturbed tree need not be the rounded product tree: its exact leaf sum accounts for the entire recursively rounded computation.',
 'targets':[
  {'name':p+'roundedDotProduct_exists_perturbation','statement':'For every model M and every tree T in Tree(R x R), let u = M.u and d = depth(T). If (d+1)u < 1 (with d+1 cast from the natural numbers to the reals), there exists P in Tree(R) such that IsPerturbation(gamma(d+1,u), exactProductTree(T), P) and exactSum(P) = roundedDotProduct(M,T). Here gamma(k,u) = (ku)/(1-ku), exactSum recursively adds the two child sums using exact real addition and returns the leaf value at a leaf, and IsPerturbation(b,A,P) means that A and P have identical ordered binary shape and every pair of corresponding real leaf values a,p satisfies |p-a| <= b|a|. Thus each leaf (x,y) of T corresponds to a leaf p of P satisfying |p-xy| <= ((d+1)u/(1-(d+1)u))|xy|. The right-hand side is the actual computation that rounds each leaf product and each internal addition. There are no further hypotheses on T or its leaf values.'},
  {'name':p+'roundedProductTerm.eq_1','statement':'For every model M and every x,y in R, roundedProductTerm(M,x,y) = M.mul(x,y). By the supplied definitions this common value is M.round(xy), the value placed at the corresponding leaf of roundedProductTree(M,T). No additional hypotheses are imposed.'},
  {'name':p+'roundedProductTree.eq_1','statement':'For every model M and every T in Tree(R x R), roundedProductTree(M,T) = map((x,y) -> roundedProductTerm(M,x,y), T). The map replaces each leaf pair by M.round(xy) and preserves every ordered binary node. No additional hypotheses are imposed.'},
  {'name':p+'roundedProductTree_isPerturbation','statement':'For every model M and every T in Tree(R x R), IsPerturbation(M.u, exactProductTree(T), roundedProductTree(M,T)). Equivalently, these two constructed real-leaf trees have the same ordered binary shape and for every corresponding input leaf (x,y), |M.round(xy)-xy| <= M.u |xy|. No depth restriction or hypothesis M.u < 1 is present.'},
  {'name':'Research.FloatingPoint.Model.mul.eq_1','statement':'For every model M and every a,b in R, M.mul(a,b) = M.round(ab), where ab is exact real multiplication. This is the multiplication used by roundedProductTerm and hence at each leaf of roundedProductTree and roundedDotProduct. No additional hypotheses are imposed.'}
 ],
 'constructions':[
  {'name':p+'exactProductTree','description':'A function Tree(R x R) -> Tree(R). It maps each leaf (x,y) to the real leaf xy using exact multiplication and preserves all internal ordered binary nodes: E(leaf(x,y)) = leaf(xy) and E(node(L,R)) = node(E(L),E(R)). It produces a tree of pairwise products; it performs no multiplication between child trees and no addition. Its exact leaf sum is the sum of the pairwise products. It is the reference tree in both perturbation targets.'},
  {'name':p+'roundedDotProduct','description':'A function Model -> Tree(R x R) -> R. For a model M with rounding function r it is roundedSum(M,roundedProductTree(M,T)). Equivalently F_M(leaf(x,y)) = r(xy) and F_M(node(L,R)) = r(F_M(L)+F_M(R)). roundedSum itself returns a real leaf value unchanged and at each internal node applies M.add(a,b) = r(a+b) to the recursively computed child values. Thus every leaf product and every internal addition is rounded, according to the supplied input tree shape. The construction neither chooses nor balances that shape. The existential target represents this scalar as an exact sum of a suitably perturbed exact-product tree under (depth(T)+1)M.u < 1.'},
  {'name':p+'roundedProductTree','description':'A function Model -> Tree(R x R) -> Tree(R). For M with rounding function r, Q_M(leaf(x,y)) = leaf(r(xy)) and Q_M(node(L,R)) = node(Q_M(L),Q_M(R)). This is map((x,y) -> roundedProductTerm(M,x,y),T), where roundedProductTerm(M,x,y) = M.mul(x,y) = r(xy). It only rounds individual leaf products and preserves the ordered binary shape; it does not reduce or add the leaves. The unconditional perturbation target bounds its leaf errors relative to exactProductTree(T) by M.u, and roundedDotProduct subsequently reduces this tree by rounded addition.'}
 ],
 'assumptions':[
  'All model, tree, real-number and natural-number variables in the target statements are universally quantified except the explicitly existential perturbed tree. Existential rounding errors delta are real and may depend on the real argument z.',
  'A model carries u in R, a proof that 0 <= u, a function round: R -> R, and the property: for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and round(z) = z(1+delta). No upper bound on u, discrete representable set, particular rounding rule, or independence of rounding errors is supplied.',
  'Tree(A) is the inductive type generated by leaf(a) for a in A and node(L,R) for L,R in Tree(A): finite, nonempty, ordered binary trees, with labels only at leaves. No balance, fixed leaf count, or fixed depth is assumed. map acts on leaf labels and preserves nodes.',
  'depth(leaf(a)) = 0 and depth(node(L,R)) = 1 + max(depth(L),depth(R)). exactSum(leaf(a)) = a and exactSum(node(L,R)) = exactSum(L) + exactSum(R), with real addition.',
  'IsPerturbation(b,A,B), for real b and real-leaf trees A,B, is generated by the leaf condition |y-x| <= b|x| and by combining two related left subtrees and two related right subtrees with the same b. Consequently it requires identical ordered binary shape and precisely these corresponding-leaf bounds. Its definition itself does not require b >= 0.',
  'gamma has domain N x R and value gamma(k,u) = (ku)/(1-ku), where k is cast to R. The existential target alone assumes (depth(T)+1)u < 1; together with u >= 0 this makes its denominator positive and its bound nonnegative. Each leaf value x,y may be any real number, including zero or negative values.'
 ],
 'missing_context':[]
}
assert [v['name'] for v in obj['targets']]==data['targets']
assert [v['name'] for v in obj['constructions']]==data['construction_names']
fd,path=tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='.translation.',suffix='.json',dir='/output')
with os.fdopen(fd,'w') as f:
    json.dump(obj,f,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2)
    f.write('\\n')
    f.flush()
    os.fsync(f.fileno())
os.replace(path,'/output/translation.json')
print('Saved /output/translation.json with all 5 targets and 3 constructions; status complete.')
PY"
